text:
At 19, Matthew Schaefer has already played 100 NHL games, and he marked the 100th with a power-play goal in Los Angeles. The reigning Calder Trophy winner leads the Islanders with 18 points in 18 games (6 goals, 12 assists) and plays 27:02 a night, a workload that has Yahoo Sports writing about his durability and endurance.

Nothing about the scoring looks borrowed. His 6 goals come on 4.6 expected, his teammates have actually scored a little less than their chances with him on the ice, and New York takes 52.5% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays. Our numbers have him running hot over his last ten games, with his minutes up more than two a night.

The long view is striking too. Of the 13 defensemen picked first to third overall since 2005, the typical first full season produced 0.35 points a game. Schaefer had 59 points in 82 games as a rookie and is at a point a game now.

What to watch: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found 36% of his shots came off the rush last season, about double the typical defenseman. He joins the attack early.
